source.title: Biological Plausibility and Representational Alignment of Feedback Alignment in Convolutional Networks

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity with linear CKA, comparing feedback-alignment methods with backpropagation. It tests partial representational alignment, but not convergence as model scale or capability increases.
record.gate_note: The study compares one CNN architecture trained on CIFAR-10 using different learning rules. It reports CKA outcomes and qualitative feature visualizations relevant to alignment. Accuracy, gradient alignment, and sign concordance are reported but do not directly measure the claim's representational convergence. The study does not test scale, cross-modal alignment, independent initializations, or representational mapping.
record.test_reason: The study measures CKA similarity to BP for one five-layer CNN on CIFAR-10, trained with different credit-assignment rules. All models share the architecture, data, loss and initialization seed (42). That is not what any version names. V1 needs independently trained models differing in architecture, objective or data, across scale. V3 needs different initializations. V2 and V4 are absent. The V5 analysis is a hand-picked qualitative view of top channels with no feature matching. The V6 subset comparison is qualitative only and uses a single metric. V7 concerns plateauing, and shared data or objectives as the cause, which the study does not examine. Because the seed is shared, high CKA cannot be credited to convergence rather than common initialization. The finding is real, but it concerns a related construct, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that uSF methods reach near-perfect early-layer agreement with BP, while standard FA learns structurally different solutions. The degree of convergence tracks the biological-plausibility cost layer by layer. Modified FA's success is rooted in approximating BP's solution, not a novel credit-assignment strategy.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares feedback-alignment learning rules and BP using linear CKA on one shared CNN and dataset. It does not reproduce a scale sweep or cross-architecture, cross-objective, or cross-modal alignment test.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note that CKA depends on the comparison set and layer granularity. They report the same qualitative pattern across the tested input subsets; alternative similarity metrics and out-of-distribution inputs are not tested.

fits_no_version.finding: Same architecture, data and seed, differing only in credit-assignment rule. Higher-accuracy rules are much closer to BP. uSF variants (74–76% test) reach CKA 0.99 at conv1 and 0.93–0.94 at conv2, and 0.75–0.87 in FC layers. Pure FA variants (36–40% test) reach 0.60–0.72 at conv1 and 0.06–0.09 at fc3. The pattern is described as holding across three input subsets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks trained with different learning rules from a shared initialization converge on BP-like representations to the extent they match BP's task performance and gradient alignment. Early layers converge more than later ones.

fits_no_version.finding: For dog-important Conv2 channels, uSF Init's top images resemble BP's (small dogs). uSF SN's top channels respond to birds, ships and planes despite near-BP accuracy. FA channels respond to luminance or lack dog specificity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High layer-level CKA can coexist with different class-specific feature pathways (uSF SN).

record.problems: Evidence is limited to one five-layer CNN architecture and CIFAR-10. The authors report a limited number of training runs and say further replication would strengthen confidence. CKA results are sensitive to comparison set and layer granularity; most CKA outcomes are qualitative, and no uncertainty estimates are given.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant CKA or feature-visualization results were omitted. Accuracy, gradient-alignment, and sign-concordance results were not entered because they do not measure representational convergence.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep. No independently trained models differing in architecture, objective or data.
No vision–language models or paired data.
All models share one initialization seed. No cross-seed comparison.
No linear maps, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment.
No matching of neurons, SAE features or circuits across models. Only a qualitative top-channel view.
Only linear CKA is used. No alternative metrics, no neighbour settings, no out-of-distribution inputs. Subset comparison is qualitative only.
No plateau over scale. No test of shared data or objectives as the cause of alignment.

missing.what: Test accuracy per method (BP 75.80, FA Random 35.77, FA Toeplitz 40.07, uSF Init 74.30, uSF SN 75.67). Needed to relate alignment to capability in the fits_no_version finding.

record.verdict_notes: The shared initialization seed is a major confound for any convergence reading. Results come from a single run per method, with no uncertainty reported. The paper does not cite or engage the Platonic Representation Hypothesis or the convergent-learning work. The reader's V5, V6 and V7 labels are dropped because the rows do not measure those versions' constructs. The study references a code release, though no link appears in the text.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no comparison across different architectures, objectives, or data.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
The methods share an initialization seed; the study does not compare independently initialized networks or shared subspaces across seeds.
CKA similarity is measured, but the study does not test mapping, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
The feature visualization is limited to selected dog-relevant Conv2 channels and top-activating CIFAR-10 images; it does not test recurrence of circuits or SAE features.
The study compares several input subsets qualitatively, but does not compare alternative similarity metrics, vary the number of neighbours, or test out-of-distribution inputs.
It reports incomplete alignment across layers and methods, but does not test whether alignment plateaus over scale or isolate shared data/objectives as a cause versus a common model of reality.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Pure FA variants, especially deeper layers
reader_labels.reason: FA variants have low layer-matched CKA, with reported fc3 values of 0.09 and 0.06, and the main subset analysis describes near-zero deeper similarity (r2, r4, r11, r12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The uSF variants reach 0.99 CKA at conv1 and high similarity at conv2, although their fully connected layers are less aligned (r5-r10, r13, r14).
